title: Introduction
content:
Serverless Function Monitoring This project focuses on deploying, monitoring, and optimizing an AWS Lambda function to ensure performance and cost efficiency for a serverless system. Through integration with Amazon CloudWatch and Amazon SNS, the project provides an overview of the number of invocations, execution time, errors, cold starts, and operating costs of the Lambda function.
Users will:
Create and optimize a Lambda function using Python. Enable Lambda Insights to analyze cold starts. Build a visual CloudWatch Dashboard to monitor performance. Set up an email alert system when there is a problem or cost threshold is exceeded. By applying monitoring and alerting techniques, this project helps users to be proactive in operating serverless services and ensure the stability and continuity of the system in a real environment.

title: Preparing Lambda
content:
Introduction AWS Lambda is a serverless computing service that lets you run code without provisioning or managing servers. You just write code, and Lambda automatically takes care of scaling, availability, and failure handling.
Why AWS Lambda? AWS Lambda lets you run code for almost any type of application or backend service without provisioning or managing servers. Simply upload your code as a Lambda function, and the service automatically takes care of the rest. Lambda supports a variety of programming languages, including Python, Node.js, Java, Go, and more. Lambda integrates tightly with other AWS services like Amazon S3, DynamoDB, API Gateway, and CloudWatch so you can build complete, scalable, and cost-effective applications. With its time-of-execution and request-based pricing model, Lambda is ideal for volatile, volatile workloads.
Benefits of AWS Lambda No Server Management: Automatically deploy and scale functions based on request volume. You don’t need to worry about configuring, patching, or maintaining servers.
Low Cost, Resource-Optimized: Pay only for the actual time your code runs and the number of function calls. No cost when not in use.
Elastic Scalability: Automatically scale based on request volume, from a few requests/second to thousands without intervention.
Easy integration with other AWS services: Easily build event-driven applications, handle real-time, automate workflows with services such as S3, DynamoDB, SNS, API Gateway…
To learn more about AWS Lambda, you can refer to the website below described

title: Clean up resources
content:
We will take the following steps to delete the resources we created in this exercise.
Delete AWS Lambda Go to Lambda console Click Functions. Tick the data related to the lab. On the right corner, click Action. Select delete. Delete AWS CloudWatch. Go to Amazon CloudWatch Click Dashboards. Select the data related to the lab. Select delete. 1.1 Then go to All alarms on the left sidebar.
Select the data related to the lab. On the right corner, click Action then select delete. 1.2 Continue to select Log groups on the left sidebar.
Select all data related to the lab. On the right corner, click Action then select delete. Delete AWS SNS Go to Amazon SNS Select Topic. Select the topics created in the lab. Select delete Then select subscriptions. Select the subscriptions created in the lab. Select delete Delete IAM Policy Go to IAM Select Policies. Tick the data related to the lab. Then select delete
